preamble: Devoicing of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] combined with retraction to the uvular region yields [χ]. The best-documented cases are in Low Franconian: in the Netherlands, northern Standard Dutch largely realizes /ɣ/ like /x/, as a voiceless post-velar or uvular fricative (the so-called 'harde g'), and Afrikaans completed the change, having no /ɣ/ at all, so that Dutch g-words appear with /χ/.

examples.note: In the north, /ɣ/ is often realized the same as /x/, as a voiceless post-velar [x̠] or uvular [χ] fricative; southern (Belgian and southern Netherlands) varieties keep voiced, more fronted /ɣ/.
The phonemes are not fully merged: the past-tense suffix still follows the underlying voicing (loogde 'leached' vs lachte 'laughed').
Afrikaans has no /ɣ/; former /ɣ/ and /x/ fell together as /χ/, most often uvular [χ] (sometimes a voiceless uvular trill).

sources: Gussenhoven, C. (1992). Dutch. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 22(1-2), 45-47. https://doi.org/10.1017/S002510030000459X
Collins, B., & Mees, I. M. (2003). The Phonetics of English and Dutch (5th ed.). Brill.
Donaldson, B. C. (1993). A Grammar of Afrikaans. Mouton de Gruyter.
